plans.note: Sec 21.1 caps liability at one month of Fees 'without exception', which conflicts with the Excluded Claims in 21.3 and is far below a meaningful cap — likely deviation. Check 21.2 (consequential damages, direct-damage carve-ins) and 21.3/21.4 for carve-out adequacy.

Section 20 heading contains only 20.1, a broad Customer-gives indemnity; no Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity appears. Note Sec 9.3 cross-references 'Section 20.5' (remedies for infringement) which does not exist — flag missing Vendor indemnity plus overbroad Customer indemnity.
Sec 12.4 imposes a 24-month post-term non-compete on Customer — direct breach. Sec 12.3 is the pro-Customer clause that contradicts it; reconcile by deleting 12.4.
Sec 2.2 (first of the two 2.2s) makes Vendor sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics — deviation. Sec 12.3 disclaims exclusivity; note the internal conflict.
No MFN obligation on Customer found; Sec 12.3 expressly disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment. Confirm against pricing sections 7.1 and 8.3 before marking absent.
No non-solicit binding Customer; Sec 12.3 confirms no no-hire commitment and preserves general-recruitment hiring. Likely compliant/absent.

Sec 9.4 gives Customer 30-day convenience termination with refunds and denies Vendor a matching right — favourable. Cross-check Sec 2.1 take-or-pay 'without reduction or termination rights', which undercuts 9.4 (address primarily under MINCOMMIT).
Sec 8.2 gives 30-day non-renewal notice plus a 60-day reminder with deadline extension; Sec 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3%. Likely compliant.
New York law and New York County courts, no foreign arbitration — likely compliant; note pre-suit executive escalation in 28.3 does not bar urgent relief.
Sec 24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor; 24.4 blocks Vendor termination/repricing on our change of control. Likely compliant.

Sec 14.1–14.2 give Customer ownership of Customer Data and assigned Deliverables; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology with a perpetual licence back. Verify no data/IP assignment to Vendor and check Sec 15.1 model-training restriction.

Sec 13.1 grants a licence to Customer alone, excluding Affiliates and contractors, and revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — deviation. Sec 13.2/13.3 (perpetual paid-up licence, limited revocation) are the reconciling provisions to cite.

Sec 22.1 limits audits to once yearly with 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable; 22.2 puts cost on Vendor absent >5% underpayment. Likely compliant; Sec 23 (records) may hold related assurance obligations.

No liquidated damages or penalty payable by Customer identified; Sec 7.3 bars interest on amounts not due and 9.4 says termination is penalty-free. Take-or-pay exposure in Sec 2.1 is handled under MINCOMMIT.

Sec 19.2 limits the Deliverable conformity warranty to 15 days with no correction or refund thereafter — likely deviation on duration. Sec 19.1/19.3 warranties and the 19.4 re-perform/refund remedy are the supporting provisions.
Sec 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, E&O and USD 5M cyber cover; 18.2 adds certificates and non-limitation of liability. Likely compliant.

Sec 2.1 imposes USD 2M/year take-or-pay for three years with no reduction or termination rights — deviation. Cite conflict with Sec 9.4 convenience termination and Sec 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement.

Sec 11.1 requires immediate cessation of assistance and deletion with no export — deviation, and it contradicts Sec 11.2/11.3 (30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion). Propose deleting 11.1 and adding a transition-assistance period.
